name: b-crayon-closeup-hands
prompt: Vertical waist-up close shot of two people sharing a wooden park bench, rendered as an old newspaper opinion-page drawing: broad, broken strokes of black lithographic grease crayon scrubbed over coarse off-white paper so the tooth shows through, with puddled washes of thinned India ink and a few scratched-out white highlights. Nearest to us, square in the middle, a fleshy hand in a pale kid glove is lifted palm outward in a lazy brush-off gesture; it is drawn hard and exact, every knuckle crease outlined in firm dark line, the crispest mark on the page. Just past that hand, rendered in gentler, half-dissolved crayon with rubbed edges, a worn-out present-day nurse in creased scrubs leans toward him, lips parted mid-word, fingers spread flat on her breastbone, a plastic hospital pass on a lanyard at her chest, eyebrows pulled together. He sits to the right: a heavy, well-fed gentleman with a high black top hat, starched wing collar and a watch chain stretched across a bulging waistcoat, nose lifted, lids lowered, gazing straight ahead as though she were not there. A low raking light comes from the left, leaving her cheekbone and his raised glove as bare paper, while everything toward the right edge drowns in thick, waxy, glossy crayon black that eats into his frock coat. Across the lowest strip of the composition runs a trimmed hedge, a dark mass of quick zigzag crayon scribble with nothing in front of it, kept clear for words to be added later. Monochrome only: crayon black, ink greys and the warm white of the paper. Leave out all lettering, balloons, labels and signatures. Thanks.
